difficulty.notes: Readable (non-minified) inline login script in login.html. Anchor is the anonymous $.get token success callback that double-SHA1s the password with a server nonce/ts. The SHA-1 primitive lives in a separate, fully-commented sha1.js (Sha1.hash) — conceptually the 0.5 utility but not pinned as a role row. Decoys are page search-bar helpers in the same file. doyo/cnzz/baidu analytics are vendor noise.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The $.get token success callback that computes pwd=Sha1.hash(nonce+ts+Sha1.hash(raw)) and posts it; not the generic Sha1.hash primitive or page/search helpers.

behavior_category.subtype: double SHA-1 of password salted with server nonce+ts
behavior_category.recompute_check: The salt (nonce, ts) is issued by the server per attempt; the final hash is not reproducible offline to a fixed value.

near_categories.why_not: Only the single password field is hashed; the request body is not otherwise transformed.
The token derives from the password + server nonce, not from device/browser signals.

evidence: The callback also reads nonce/ts and assembles the full $.post payload (username, remember, etc.); only the password derivation is the target.
The password value is finalized inside a nested $.get success callback, two callbacks deep from the submit click, using a SHA-1 routine in a separate file.

answer_match.notes: 1.json case 17 begins at the same $.get('/User/Passport/token') call and anonymous success callback represented by oracle.primary_anchor. The oracle uses explicit offsets for that complete callback.

question_direction.notes: The visible question asks for the function whose own body combines fetched nonce/ts with the hashed password and posts it. It also excludes the generic SHA-1 primitive and unrelated page/search helpers, so it points to the anonymous token callback.

role_diversity.notes: 0.7 covers the enclosing login submit handler; 0.5 covers Sha1.hash and supporting SHA-1/UTF-8 primitives; 0.2 covers jQuery get/post/ajax wrappers, Enter-key trigger and login post response callback; 0 covers search/header decoys.
